prompt: In which year was PI Coresight renamed PI Vision?
explanation: OSIsoft states: "PI Coresight was renamed PI Vision in 2017". 2011 is when Coresight was first released.

prompt: PI WebParts were used to build PI composite applications in which platform?
explanation: PI WebParts were OSIsoft web parts for building PI composite applications in Microsoft SharePoint. Excel is PI DataLink's host.

prompt: Where does PI Manual Logger store settings and entered data before it is sent to the PI Data Archive?

options.text: In the PI Buffer Subsystem queue

explanation: PI Manual Logger stores settings and data in SQL Server "before it gets sent to PI Data Archive", so that database needs backing up.

prompt: Which browser technology did early PI Coresight clients use?
explanation: The 2011 material says "Silverlight Available from PI Coresight server, no internet access".

prompt: Which products did OSIsoft list in the PI Visualization Suite in 2017? Select all that apply.
explanation: The 2017 PI 101 deck lists PI Vision, PI ProcessBook, PI DataLink and PI WebParts in the suite. PI Manual Logger appears under PI Interfaces and PI Connectors.

prompt: How was PI Coresight positioned when it was announced in 2011?

options.text: As a new product for ad hoc analysis and collaboration that did not replace any existing product
As the immediate replacement for PI ProcessBook
As a replacement for PI DataLink

explanation: The 2011 slide calls it a "New Product – does not replace any existing PI System product", positioned for ad hoc analysis and collaboration alongside ProcessBook and WebParts.

prompt: What did PI Coresight 2016 add, according to the 2016 roadmap? Select all that apply.
explanation: PI Coresight 2016 added a new Display Editor, mobile support and Event Comparison. OpenID Connect came with PI Vision in the 2023 era.

prompt: Which PI Manual Logger clients were current in 2015?

options.text: PI ML Web 2014 / 2014 R2 and PI ML Mobile 2012

explanation: The 2015 user-conference session lists PI ML Web 2014 / 2014 R2 and PI ML Mobile 2012.

scenario: A site's SharePoint intranet shows PI dashboards built with PI WebParts. The IT team wants to know whether to invest in them for the next five years.

options.text: WebParts appears among deprecated products no longer sold, so plan to rebuild in PI Vision and confirm status with AVEVA
WebParts is AVEVA's strategic dashboard product
WebParts was renamed PI Vision in 2017
WebParts is part of CONNECT data services

explanation: A 2022 feedback post lists PI WebParts among deprecated products "not being sold anymore", and a 2015 roadmap put dashboards in the future column. No official end date was found, so confirm with AVEVA. It was Coresight, not WebParts, that became PI Vision.
verifyNote: Deprecated status comes from a user-written feedback post; no official AVEVA lifecycle statement was read.
